description: Chewy clear rice noodles in a sweet pork-bone broth with sliced pork, shrimp, quail eggs and crisp fried shallots: the southern noodle soup, sold from a cart that announces itself by clacking two bamboo sticks.
A sizzling crêpe of rice flour and turmeric, folded over pork, shrimp and bean sprouts.  You wrap it in mustard leaves and dip it in sweet fish sauce.
Fresh spring rolls: rice paper wrapped around vermicelli, shrimp, pork and herbs, with a peanut and hoisin dip.  Eaten cold, and best eaten soon.
A banana-leaf packet of sticky rice with mung bean, fried shallots and a sprinkle of crushed peanuts and sugar, the breakfast every school child bought on the way to class.
A fluffy white steamed bun stuffed with pork, a slice of Chinese sausage and a quail egg, sold warm from a steamer on the back of a bicycle.
Khô mực: a whole flattened, sun-dried squid, the classic snack with beer.  Toast it over coals and tear it into chewy strips.
Tôm khô: a bag of small, salty orange dried shrimp, a pinch of which flavours a whole pot of soup.
Bánh tráng: a brittle round sheet of sun-dried rice paper, criss-crossed with the imprint of the bamboo mat it dried on.  Wet it to roll gỏi cuốn, or grill it into a snack.
